Original draft: the analytic bound `q < 10^10`, followed by an exact finite
exclusion yielding the nine class-number-one discriminants.

This release points to the original published commit
`b30549663b6d2660b2df3c916822802774e2486d`. Its proof, code, recorded outputs,
and bundle are unchanged.

- [Original proof](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.1.0/output/pdf/proof.pdf)
- [Original README and reproduction instructions](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/tree/v0.1.0)
- [Review record](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.2.0/REVIEW.md)

The analytic input is Banks's Theorem 1.1 for conductors at least `10^10`.
The repository owner subsequently reported a cross-check of the original
mathematical argument with a different frontier model. That report does
not change the preserved snapshot, and no detailed review report is bundled.

This is an AI-assisted research draft, published as a prerelease for review.
The two sieve algorithms were written by the same assistant. The project
does not independently establish Banks's theorem.
